[h1]Review – Never Again[/h1]

[b]Overall Impression:[/b]
Never Again is a short horror puzzle game that mainly has decent graphics going for it, but doesn’t really do anything meaningful with them. It’s not particularly scary, and the atmosphere never fully develops. Instead, the game feels like a missed opportunity, especially with how the story is handled and presented.

[hr]
[h2]Pros[/h2]

[list]
[][b]Okay graphics:[/b] Visuals are the strongest part of the game.
[][b]Short playtime:[/b] Quick to finish (around 2–3 hours depending on puzzle frustration).
[/list]

[hr]
[h2]Cons[/h2]

[list]
[][b]Not really scary:[/b] Despite being a horror game, it rarely feels tense or frightening.
[][b]Wasted atmosphere:[/b] Good visuals, but nothing meaningful is done with them.
[][b]Confusing puzzles:[/b] Unnecessarily unclear and frustrating progression.
[][b]Weak storytelling:[/b] The story feels poorly executed and ends up focusing on WWII victim themes in a way that feels forced.
[/list]

[hr]

[h2]Recommendation[/h2]
Not worth it, even on sale. Good graphics alone can’t save the weak gameplay, lack of horror, and disappointing story execution.

Franchement c'est dommage, le jeu est super à plein de points de vue : ambiance et réalisation, histoire avec une dimension historique sérieuse (c'est pas juste de l'horreur gratuite), puzzles assez riches et imaginatifs... Mais pour moi il y a un réel problème d'équilibre au niveau des phases de boss qui malheureusement ruine le jeu, problème qui pourrait sans doute être réglé très simplement en réduisant un peu la fréquence d'apparition des boss. 

Car dans ces phases il faut : 
- explorer et fouiller l'environnement à la lampe de poche (on est plongé dans la semi-obscurité)
- comprendre le mécanisme à activer
- trouver les différents éléments permettant d'activer le mécanisme 
- tester des trucs pour comprendre la subtilité qui va faire que le mécanisme fonctionne, car les éléments trouvés, tout seuls, ne suffisent pas forcément
- et tout cela en se faisant pourchasser par un boss qui dès qu'il nous voit, nous fonce dessus sans réelle possibilité de lui échapper à ce stade (et j'ai pas trop compris, par exemple dans la phase de miroirs avec la femme effrayante, si elle spawnait aléatoirement ou si on était censé pouvoir suivre son déplacement et élaborer une stratégie. Mais bon de toute façon, on n'a pas le temps d'y réfléchir). 

Alors d'un côté c'est intelligemment fait car la simulation du stress est vraiment efficace : la simple présence de ce boss fait qu'on perd nos moyens et qu'on a vachement de mal à se concentrer sur ce qu'on doit faire (qui est pas si compliqué en fait). Mais bon le problème c'est qu'à force c'est vraiment bloquant, sur la phase avec l'espèce de gros bébé par exemple, au bout d'un moment le stress ne vient plus de la simulation de la peur du personnage, mais de l'agacement du joueur : la progression ne dépend plus de votre habileté ou de votre intelligence, mais d'un déséquilibre du jeu qui fait qu'on n'a pas le temps de réfléchir et qu'on a besoin de trop d'essais pour y arriver. Ce ne sont pas des phases de combat, c'est toujours de l'énigme/réflexion/exploration de l'environnement, donc il faudrait avoir du temps pour agir... En plus c'est dommage car quand le boss nous attrape, au lieu de revenir direct au checkpoint il y a une petite phase "intermède" qui apporte un éclairage sur l'histoire et je trouve que c'est une bonne idée car ça donne du sens au fait de perdre / respawner (un truc un peu "méta"), eh bien du coup ça devient juste hyper énervant de se taper ça en plus à chaque fois !! 

Autant sur la phase "gros bébé", une fois regardée la soluce (parce que j'ai pas envie de passer ma vie à m'énerver sur ce jeu) ça passait, mais sur la phase "miroirs" (qui franchement est une super idée en plus et j'avais vraiment envie de la finir !), j'ai fini par craquer - la fréquence d'apparition du boss ne laisse vraiment pas le temps de tester des trucs, par exemple comprendre à quoi sert la toile pour se cacher (la boss me trouve quand même...), fouiller un peu plus l'environnement... On n'a déjà pas le temps pour faire ce qu'il y a à faire, et autant le bébé finissait par être juste ridicule, autant la bonne femme est carrément flippante, c'est un jump scare à chaque fois, et voir cette image encore et encore... ben à force je me sens pas très très bien. 

Pendant ce temps, mes ventilateurs tournent à donf (je joue sur PC portable)

À regret j'ai donc décidé d'épargner mes nerfs, ma carte graphique et ma batterie et de passer à autre chose... Je mets tout de même une évaluation positive car l'ambiance du jeu est vraiment à mon goût et j'aurais aimé le finir. Si j'avais un ordi plus puissant et moins vieux, et plus de temps devant moi, j'aurais sans doute persévéré mais là vu le contexte c'est too much pour moi. 

[je précise que je joue sur un PC portable avec Nvidia GeForce GTX 950M]

Gráficamente este juego es una aberración, pensé que era mucho más antiguo y me sorprende que al año en que escribo esta reseña no ha llegado ni a cumplir una década.

Por otro lado, las mecánicas no se quedan atrás, la mayor parte del tiempo se vuelven aburridas y repetitivas en un juego con una duración de menos de dos horas. Y por su puesto, su peor error son los puntos de spawn y la nula explicación de los niveles.

La explicación se puede deducir y descubrir mientras juegas, así que no existe problema más que un momento de frustración de vez en cuando, pero los spawns son horrorosos, muchas veces perdí por culpa de ello. También la inteligencia artificial del juego es horrible, la mayor parte del tiempo estará campeando en el objetivo y te impedirá continuar avanzando.

Creo que pesé al trillado tema, es una historia decente que retrata muy bien los horrores que se tuvieron que vivir, lastimosamente mucho de ello se queda en unos coleccionables por qué al parecer es la única forma en que los videojuegos pueden contarte su historia y transfondo, además de su nulo soporte al español, que no le perjudica, pero si es un detalle que se apreciaría.

Pero, si me sentiría estafado si no lo hubiese comprado en oferta, pues aunque tiene un precio bajo normalmente, siento que tanto su duración, sus mecánicas, su ia, su historia, sus gráficos y sus animaciones, si dejan mucho a deber, básicamente, lo terminas porque ya lo compraste, no porque realmente te llame la atención.

A rather scattered horror game somewhat in the vein of Layers of Fear, but with fewer jump scares and more puzzles, some logic, some find the object(s). The most difficult parts involve having to solve the logic puzzles while someone is chasing you, which really ramps up the difficulty, and for me ramps down the enjoyment. At least you don’t lose any progress when you are caught & die; you are just forced to navigate a 15-second maze to get back. Which is good because when you pop out of the maze there’s a decent chance it will be in the same location where the killer is and you'll have to do it all over again 1 second later. Ugh.

The object puzzles are standard video game fare. EG find all of the things you need to light a fire in the fireplace. Deep Stuff, and Entirely Relevant to the storyline. This part was somewhat buggy at least for me, with some of the objects refusing to let me pick them up and move them more than a foot. Luckily restarting the game fixed this bug.

I suspect that the relatively high number of positive reviews has something to do with the storyline. While it is interesting, I find it rather clumsily told, and honestly it feels a bit like it was tacked on after the game was mostly finished. A lot of the gameplay seems to be fairly irrelevant to the main plot. Even with that criticism, however, the story is better than in a lot of these sorts of games.

In the end, I can’t really recommend this unless you enjoy solving puzzles while being chased. That aspect of the game is only about a third of the time I spent in it, but it was easily the most frustrating part. If what is frustrating to me sounds appealing to you, then I think this game is decent, especially on sale. However, I do not come away feeling like it was a very good use of my time, even if it had been free.

I really don't like being negative but I am honest.    

I'll start with mechanics.  I played on PC with mouse and keyboard.  I believe the game play itself would have been much easier using a controller.  I tried using a controller toward the end of the game but it did not work even though the game does list full controller support for Xbox controllers.   Using  a mouse and keyboard was excruciatingly painful at times.  It literally started to give me a headache more than once.  Pushing and pulling objects, moving objects in puzzles, etc. with the kb and mouse felt like a chore that required much more effort than it should.

Next up is the puzzles.  Aside from the last one, they were not at all intuitive.  While there are features to help in guiding the way, they do not make up for the lack of intuitiveness.

Then there is the inhaler.  An item "needed" to keep your character alive.  Others have mentioned they ran out and were unable to find any more.  I found that it was only actually needed for three instances as there is another item (flashlight) which can be used instead and never runs out of batteries.  As for the inhaler itself, it didn't add to the story in a meaningful way even though the character (Sasha) has asthma, which is supposed to be a big part of the story.

Lastly is the story, which was lackluster at best.  I won't go into details of the story as it is very short.  There are two one-shot "bosses" that had nothing to do with the story.  I suppose they could be thought of as side stories but very thin ones.  While I do appreciate the story the devs were trying to tell, it just wasn't very cohesive.  I won't spoil the ending, although at this point in time, it is unlikely there are many new players, so I'll just say it was a huge letdown and not at all satisfying. In conclusion, if you are going to play this game, I recommend using a controller and having a lot of patience.

[h2]Never Again 测评｜8.8/10：小体量但氛围很“扎”，解谜与惊吓节奏拿捏得当[/h2]

[h2]评分[/h2]
[b]8.8/10（推荐）[/b]

[h2]核心体验：心理恐怖 + 探索解谜的“沉浸型短篇”[/h2]
《Never Again》属于那种不靠血浆堆砌，而是用环境、音效与叙事压迫感把你一步步拖进阴影里的作品。官方定位本就强调“探索地点与解谜”并围绕一位患哮喘的小女孩展开剧情，这种视角与主题让故事更具情绪重量，也更容易代入。

[h2]优点[/h2]
[list]
[*][b]氛围塑造[/b]：场景与音效配合得很到位，能持续制造不安感；惊吓更多是“渐进式升温”，而不是廉价的 Jump Scare 轰炸（高赞评价里也常提到“慢慢变得更吓人”）。
[*][b]解谜与节奏[/b]：谜题整体偏轻到中等，推动探索与叙事，不太会因为解谜卡关而破坏氛围；流程紧凑，适合一口气沉浸通关。
[*][b]叙事切入点[/b]：以儿童视角与“病症（哮喘）”作为叙事元素，让恐惧不仅来自外部怪异，也来自心理与身体层面的脆弱感，属于比较少见的设计方向。
[/list]

[h2]缺点[/h2]
[list]
[*][b]部分追逐/一击必杀段落[/b]可能会让不喜欢“试错式恐怖”的玩家感到烦躁（玩家评论也提到过类似 Outlast 那种一击死的讨厌点）。
[*][b]体量与重复度[/b]：作为偏短篇的恐怖解谜，核心亮点集中在氛围与叙事推进上；如果你更偏好高强度战斗/深度系统，可能会觉得“更像体验型作品”。
[/list]

[h2]适合谁？[/h2]
[list]
[*]喜欢[b]心理恐怖 + 探索解谜[/b]、更看重氛围与故事推进的玩家
[*]想要一款节奏紧凑、沉浸感强、不会太“硬核折磨”的恐怖向作品
[/list]


[h2]一句话总结[/h2]
[b]《Never Again》是一部“以氛围和情绪压迫取胜”的恐怖解谜短篇：不一定是最吓人的，但很会让你一直不舒服地想把真相看完。[/b]

[h2]A Psychological Horror That Gets Under Your Skin[/h2]
[h3]Score: 7/10[/h3]
It's the kind that slowly, quietly, and completely messes with your head, along with some good jump scares.

You play as a little girl named Sasha, and the atmosphere is just so unsettling, in the right way. The whole game feels silent and eerie, and the story unfolds through these really abstract, puzzle-like memories.

I would say the story is good enough, but the puzzles do take over it. Concept is great!
The way it uses atmosphere and sound to build tension is a masterclass in creepy.
It's not a super-long game. Took around 7.5 hours to 100%.

Now, a heads-up: this game is pretty abstract. If you need everything to make perfect logical sense from the start, you might get a little lost, and honestly, some of the puzzles can feel like a lot to handle [mirror one for me]. 
It also doesn't really hold your hand, which can be a little frustrating. But if you can just let the story and the mood wash over you, it’s a good experience.

[b]What I didn't like:[/b] 
Controls are not smooth, especially on the keyboard and mouse, as I had to repeatedly drag things a lot for the action to get triggered, which was extremely annoying. Plus, there is no chapter replay system, which makes the missed achievements a pain to get, as you have to play the whole game again.

[h3]Final Verdict[/h3]
If you're a fan of psychological thrillers, eerie atmospheres, and puzzles that make you think, you should give this a try.
If you don't like challenging puzzles at all, then you should skip this one.

Never Again is a beautifully haunting psychological horror game that goes far beyond cheap jump scares. With its deeply emotional story, stunning atmosphere, and thought-provoking symbolism, it delivers an unforgettable experience that lingers long after the game ends.

You play as Sasha, a 13-year-old girl struggling with asthma and waking up in an empty, terrifying world. As you explore the eerie house and unravel the story piece by piece, you realize this isn't just a horror game—it's a deeply personal journey through fear, trauma, and the fragility of the human mind.

The game masterfully blends environmental storytelling with surreal, dream-like visuals to reflect Sasha’s inner struggles. The anxiety attacks, the mysterious puzzles, and the constantly shifting reality all serve to immerse the player in a world where nothing is safe—and nothing is as it seems.

What makes Never Again stand out is its emotional weight. It doesn’t just scare you—it makes you feel. The voice acting and soundtrack are minimal but effective, adding to the overall sense of isolation and dread.

In the end, Never Again is more than a horror game. It’s a meaningful story about growing up with trauma, feeling lost, and searching for hope. A hidden indie gem that deserves far more recognition.
